edges.description: DAP12-null bone marrow yields immature osteoclasts with attenuated resorption, and the mice develop increased bone mass - a direct functional demonstration of the cellular defect this node asserts.
edges.limitations: The organism-level readout diverges: mice develop osteopetrosis (uniformly increased bone mass), whereas patients develop focal lytic cysts with fragility. The cellular mechanism transfers; the tissue outcome does not.

edges.description: The mice show a reduction of myelin accentuated in the thalamus, with immature oligodendrocytes arrested nearby.
edges.limitations: The mouse lesion is a regionally restricted developmental arrest centred on the thalamus, whereas the human disease is a progressive, frontally accentuated sclerosing leukoencephalopathy in an adult brain. Distribution, timing and progressive character all differ.

edges.description: Single-nuclei profiling of mice lacking DAP12 signalling showed only very mild microglial defects and did not reproduce the human NHD microglial signature. This is a substantive negative result, not an absence of data: the same study generated the human and mouse profiles and compared them directly.
edges.limitations: The mouse does not reproduce the RUNX1/STAT3/TGF-beta wound-healing program that defines this node in human brain. Any therapeutic inference about resetting microglial signalling that rests on this mouse is therefore unsupported, and mouse-derived microglial readouts should not be used as a proxy for the human microglial state.

nodes.description: The reference genetic model. It reproduces the two tissue-level arms of the disease - a bone phenotype and a myelin phenotype - but does so with important differences from the human lesion, and the microglial state that current human data place at the centre of the CNS arm is specifically not reproduced. It is therefore a good model of the consequences and a poor model of the mechanism, which is worth stating explicitly rather than leaving a reader to infer from a citation list.

Loss of myelin already laid down, distinct from the failure to make it. Human NHD brain shows myelin loss, and the proposed sequence is that the dysregulated microglial state promotes demyelination and then fails to clear the resulting debris, which further activates microglia. Whether the demyelination is a consequence of the failed myelination node or an independent microglia-driven process is not established, which is why the edge into it is drawn with unknown intermediates.

evidence.snippet: an early-onset dementia characterized by cerebral atrophy, myelin loss and gliosis

nodes.description: The intuitive prediction from losing an activating receptor is quiescent microglia. What single-nucleus RNA sequencing of DAP12-deficient human brain actually found is the opposite: a distinctive signature of heightened RUNX1, STAT3 and TGF-beta signalling - the transcriptional program of repair responses to injury - running unchecked. The current reading is that DAP12 signalling normally restrains these wound-healing pathways, and that without that brake they crowd out the physiological functions of microglia. This is the node on which the mouse and the human diverge, and it is the least settled step in the pathograph.

nodes.description: The clinical endpoint of the CNS arm: an insidious personality change with loss of judgment, euphoria, loss of social inhibitions and lack of insight, progressing to frank dementia and loss of mobility, beginning around age 30 and causing death typically before 50. The frontal, behavioural character of the presentation is why patients are often first seen in psychiatric rather than neurological services.

The human lesion is not simply osteopetrosis, however - patients get focal cystic osteodysplasia of the small bones and epiphyses rather than a uniformly dense skeleton, so this node is modelled as failed remodelling rather than as absent resorption.

nodes.description: A failure to lay down myelin. Oligodendrocytes in DAP12-deficient human brain carry an impaired-myelination signature, and DAP12-null mice show oligodendrocyte precursors arrested near the thalamus - a developmental arrest rather than destruction of myelin already made. Whether the oligodendrocyte defect is driven entirely by the microglial state or is partly cell-autonomous is not resolved; the entry models it as downstream of the microglial node because that is what the human co-expression data support.

nodes.description: Without an intact TREM2-DAP12 pair, ligand engagement no longer phosphorylates the DAP12 ITAM, and the downstream tyrosine-kinase cascade that normally drives myeloid activation, cytoskeletal reorganisation and phagocytosis is not initiated. The same signalling failure is then read out differently by the two cell types that depend on it.

nodes.description: Failed remodelling produces well-defined lytic cysts in the carpal, tarsal, metacarpal, metatarsal and phalangeal bones and at the ends of long bones, filled with partly necrotic fatty tissue - the finding that gives the disease its "lipomembranous" name and its brain-bone-fat nickname. The cysts weaken the bone locally, which is why symptoms begin as strain-related pain at the ankles and wrists and progress to fracture on minor trauma.

nodes.description: Biallelic null or hypomorphic variants in TYROBP or TREM2 remove one half of a two-subunit myeloid immunoreceptor. TREM2 is the ligand-binding subunit, a lipid-sensing receptor whose short cytoplasmic tail carries no signalling motif of its own; DAP12 is the ITAM-bearing transmembrane adaptor that transduces for it. Losing either subunit disables the complex, which is why two genes give one disease. The complex is expressed on microglia and on osteoclasts, and that shared expression - not two separate lesions - is what couples the brain and bone arms of the phenotype.
